page: Microsoft Azure D64ds_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DDSv5 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 32 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8370C processor operating at 2.8 GHz. The architecture is x86_64 with hyper-threading enabled. System memory totals 256.0 GB, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB per core. For local storage, the instance includes a bundled 2458 GB SSD and supports Premium Storage.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core performance, with top-tier results in multi-threaded stress-ng, Geekbench, and Passmark CPU tests. Large block memory bandwidth read and write operations also rank in the top 25%. However, single-core performance remains average across stress-ng and Geekbench tests. Cryptographic capabilities are supported by hardware-accelerated instructions including AES, VAES, and SHA_NI, alongside AVX-512 vector extensions.

This server is highly capable for database operations, as demonstrated by strong Passmark database and Redis SET benchmarks of 62.19 million operations per second, as well as high static web serving throughput of 52.02 GB/sec. While it handles prompt processing for small LLM models efficiently, text generation for large 70B models is a notable bottleneck, performing in the bottom 25% with 2.72 tokens per second. The instance offers a balanced resource density, making it a cost-efficient option for multi-threaded enterprise applications, database hosting, and web serving without the overhead of dedicated GPU hardware.
description: The Microsoft Azure D64ds_v5 is an x86_64 general-purpose virtual machine from the DDSv5 family, powered by a 2.8 GHz Intel Xeon 8370C processor. It features 64 dedicated vCPUs, 256.0 GB of RAM, and a bundled 2458 GB local SSD. Operating under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, this instance delivers strong multi-core CPU performance and high memory bandwidth for large block operations. It excels in database operations, software compilation, and high-throughput web serving, though single-core performance and large-model LLM text generation represent relative performance tradeoffs. With its balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and substantial local storage, the D64ds_v5 represents a resource-dense, cost-efficient profile for enterprise workloads, multi-threaded applications, and database hosting.
